reasons: F11, F13: material related-party transactions combined with a single customer accounting for more than half of receivables creates concentration and arm's-length/collectibility risk around revenue and receivables.

F08, R19: revenue is largely recognised over time (estimate-driven) while operating cash flow is well below net income (<0.8x), a classic signal that reported earnings may be outrunning cash realisation.
F22, R13: a major acquisition in the year and a medium (50-75%) soft-asset share raise purchase-price allocation, goodwill/intangible valuation and judgment risk.
F21, R15: a capital raise in progress or planned while ROA is falling gives management an incentive to present results favourably.
F03, F24: no auditor ICFR attestation (likely a smaller filer) and no critical audit matters reported, so external control assurance is limited.
R05: slowing depreciation can indicate useful-life extensions that boost earnings.

F01, F04, F05, F07, F14, F16, F17, F19: mitigating factors are no material weakness, no going-concern doubt, no auditor change, no restatement, stable CEO/CFO, no SEC inquiry, class action or covenant problems.

R08, R17, R07, R03: negative total accruals, a Dechow F-score below threshold, stable or falling leverage and a normal asset quality index do not point to aggressive accrual manipulation; several ratios (R01, R02, R04, R09, R18) are unavailable, limiting the analysis.
